full_judgment:
6. Mr. M.A. Mannan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the court of appeal below has committed a serious error of law occasioning failure of justice in not taking into consideration the material point raised in the said appeal. He contends that the learned appellate court did not decide the question whether the pathway was used as of right or the same was being used with consent only. In support of his contention Mr. M.A. Mannan, the learned Advocate has placed before me the decision in the case of Abdul Hafiz and others Vs. Mafizuddin and others reported in 7 DLR 577. In that case it has been held that a perspective right of way cannot be acquired by mere enjoyment of the same for statutory period. The enjoyment must be as of right i.e. not attributable to permission implied or express. The mere fact that one person walks over the land of another does not raise any presumption that he has right to do so. Mr. Mannan also cited another decision in the case of Sadindee Dev Vs. Ambica Singh Manipuri and others reported in 25 DLR 327. In that decision it has been held that mere use of a pathway by a party for long cannot create prescriptive right in his favour unless it is shown that such use has been as of right peaceably and without interruption. 

 It is apparent that the mentioning in the kabala of the existence of the disputed pathway some time over 50 years back is a strong presumption that the user of the right is nothing but as of right that is to say it has a lawful origin and therefore it cannot be b brushed aside by saying that walking over other's land even for hundred years does not create any easement right.
